events.summary:
At least five taken to hospital and about 300 evacuated in strongest quake to hit southern Italian region in 40 years

At least 26 people have been injured after a 4.7-magnitude earthquake rocked a region near Naples, in southern Italy.

The quake, which occurred at 7.46pm on Friday night, caused power outages, disrupted public transport and damaged a pier in Campi Flegrei, the site of Europe’s largest volcanic crater.

events.title: Trump climbs down on Iran strikes after Saudi alarm and threats from Tehran
events.summary:
President claims delay is ‘subject to being able to rapidly make a deal’ as intervention by Saudi crown prince is revealed and Iran warns neighbours

Donald Trump said on Saturday night that the US would hold off on any new strikes on Iran provided a deal to end the months-long conflict is quickly reached – marking the president’s latest climbdown from extravagant threats to hit the Tehran regime hard.

The Saudi crown prince Mohammed bin Salman called Trump on Saturday to express concerns about his strike plans, it was reported. Trump’s reversal also came after Iran threatened to retaliate decisively against its neighbours in the event of US strikes, while Kuwait reported being hit by Iranian drones on Saturday and two ships were attacked off Oman in the strait of Hormuz.

events.title: Singapore bans Massive Attack for showing Palestinian flag, breaching ban on foreign emblems
events.summary:
Two members given ‘stern warnings’ after concert and barred from returning, with band also excluded from performing in Singapore again, say authorities

British trip-hop band Massive Attack has been barred from performing in Singapore after an investigation found two members unfurled a Palestinian flag during a concert, police said.

Singapore, known for its tough laws on public speech and assembly, bans the open display of all foreign flags, national emblems or banners without a permit.

events.summary:
The agreement is a ‘great breakthrough’, the president says in response to media questions

  • Trump claims agreement for ‘complete disarmament’ of Hamas in Gaza but support uncertain

  • Saudi Arabia prepares sea and possible land offensive against Houthis

Al Jazeera reporter Hani Mahmoud has reported the mood in Gaza this morning following news of Hamas’s potential disarmament.

Palestinians have heard repeated statements about their fate in the three years since the current war began between Israel and Hamas, so last night’s announcement by Donald Trump wasn’t met with any particular joy or celebration. “There is scepticism and cautiousness among Palestinians,” Mahoud writes from Gaza City in the north of the Strip.

events.title: World-renowned climber Nirmal Purja among 11 struck by avalanche on Pakistan mountain
events.summary:
Rescuers say four bodies found in search for team caught in Broad Peak avalanche, after trackers showed rapid descent

The world-renowned Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja – a former British special forces member – is among 11 climbers caught in a deadly avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak.

The Alpine Club of Pakistan said “seven climbers have been spotted via aerial drone footage” adding that “their identities and condition cannot yet be verified”.

events.title: Top mountaineer Nirmal Purja confirmed dead after 11 hit by avalanche in Pakistan
events.summary:
Other members of expedition led by world-renowned climber on Broad Peak also died, climbing company says

A world-renowned Nepali mountaineer and former UK Special Forces member has died after being among 11 climbers caught in a deadly avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak.

Nirmal Purja was killed leading an expedition of 10 other people on the world’s 12th-highest mountain when an avalanche struck at around noon on Thursday.

events.title: India’s monsoon rains in danger as UN chief warns planet is ‘on fire’
events.summary:
António Guterres says strengthening El Niño will help push the world’s climate crisis into ‘uncharted territory’

India’s monsoon is in danger and hotter, drier conditions are forecast across much of the world as a stronger El Niño weather system is taking hold, weather experts have warned.

António Guterres, the UN secretary general, said the strengthening El Niño was “adding fuel to a planet already on fire” and pushing the world into “uncharted territory”.

events.title: Pakistan accused of fatally shooting 30 unarmed protesters in Kashmir
events.summary:
Local civil rights group alleges authorities removed evidence of killings amid communications blackout

At least 30 people are alleged to have been killed in Pakistan-administered Kashmir in the past two days as part of what has been claimed is a brutal state crackdown that has engulfed the disputed region for weeks.

According to a local civil society group, Joint Awami Action Committee (JAAC), the Pakistani security services fired on tens of thousands of peaceful protesters, killing 25 people on Monday and five more on Tuesday.

Continue reading...

events.title: India’s Cockroach movement threatens to restart protests after mass student arrests
events.summary:
Cockroach Janta party says government has broken promise, with detentions in Delhi, Assam, West Bengal and Bihar

India’s youth-led “Cockroach” movement, whose nationwide protests forced the resignation of the education minister, has accused the government of backtracking on its promise not to act against student protesters and has threatened to restart demonstrations.

The Cockroach Janta party (CJP), which organised mass protests over exam paper leaks and other irregularities, said it had received reports of hundreds of students being detained or “harassed” by police.

Continue reading...

events.title: ‘We have lost everything’: extreme rainfall across Asia brings flash floods and typhoons
events.summary:
From Afghanistan to Taiwan, unprecedented deluge highlights devastating impact of climate breakdown

“It rained for 10 days and 10 nights, non-stop – I’d never seen anything like it,” says Anar Gul, a construction worker who lives in the remote district of Dur Baba in eastern Afghanistan.

The houses in his village are built from stone and mud, which makes them extremely vulnerable to heavy rains. After days of rain, Gul’s kitchen collapsed and his neighbour, Sayed Afsar Sadat, saw a large part of his house completely destroyed. “Rains like this are coming heavier and earlier each year,” says Sadat. “They are destroying the roads and washing away our crops. It’s impacting us directly.”

Continue reading...

events.title: Relentless UK heatwaves turn ‘green and pleasant’ land brown
events.summary:
Visible impact of warming climate is impossible to ignore across landscapes that have been starved of rainfall

Half of England and the whole of Wales are officially in drought and July is set to be the driest month on record as extreme heat intensified by the climate crisis continues to grip the UK and Europe this summer.

The announcements this week by England’s Environment Agency and Natural Resources Wales mark the third such event over the past five years, and come in the wake of four record-breaking heatwaves since May which have fuelled huge wildfires and left farmers, wildlife and protected habitats running out of water.

events.title: Stock market turmoil sheds stark light on the opaque AI economy
events.summary:
Investors scramble to make sense of a shock Chinese challenge to the dominance of western chipmakers

Even for the rollercoaster world of AI, last week was particularly volatile as investors scrambled to keep up with developments that threatened the dominance of the largest western chipmakers.

It began with a double whammy. On Monday, the Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT floated on the Shanghai stock market, soaring by 466% in value to 3.3tn yuan (£365bn).

events.title: ‘We cannot magic up more water’: the supply problems putting housing targets in England at risk
events.summary:
Council leaders say crumbling infrastructure and lack of water are jeopardising government’s plans for new homes

The government’s housebuilding agenda is hitting the stark reality of a lack of water and crumbling infrastructure across the east and south-east of England.

Half the country was declared to be in serious drought this week, for the second consecutive year, with the Environment Agency warning of dire consequences for the economy, environment and wildlife.

events.title: UK’s state investments agency hit by data breach
events.summary:
Security lapse leaves sensitive information and contact details of 51 government officials exposed for 40 hours

The public body in charge of the UK’s state investments has been pushed to improve its internal security after a data breach left “high-level management information” publicly accessible for nearly two days.

UK Government Investments (UKGI), the agency that manages the taxpayers’ interest in a swathe of companies including Channel 4 and the Post Office, said the security failure also left more than 50 government officials’ personal details exposed for nearly 40 hours.

events.title: Undercover police unit closed down over unjustified surveillance, spycops inquiry told
events.summary:
Senior officer behind closure says SDS caused ‘incalculable harm’ by infiltrating groups that posed no threat

An undercover police unit that spied on tens of thousands of political activists had to be shut down amid severe criticisms and recriminations, the spycops public inquiry has heard.

Jon Boutcher, a senior police officer who took over responsibility for the Special Demonstration Squad (SDS) unit, concluded within months that it had to be wound up because it was conducting unjustified surveillance and was badly run.

Continue reading...

events.title: US officials focus on identification and rapid action as measles cases rise
events.summary:
Authorities in Delaware tackle cluster with vaccination and contract tracing – but field has been weakened by cuts

Measles outbreaks are igniting throughout the United States as the nation passes the highest case count in 30 years – putting greater pressure on state and local health departments and highlighting the importance of early identification and quick action.

The US has officially surpassed last year’s tally of measles cases, reaching 2,371 confirmed infections by the end of July. Those numbers have been driven by clusters in Arizona, South Carolina, and Utah – but in times of high transmission, outbreaks elsewhere become more likely. And with decreasing vaccination rates across the country, these sparks are falling on increasingly dry timber.

events.title: Shooting at In-N-Out Burger restaurant in Idaho leaves three people dead
events.summary:

Police who responded to the shooting found the body of the suspected gunman in an area near the restaurant, Twin Falls city public information officer Josh Palmer said. He did not know if the suspect was included in the fatality count.

events.title: Capital One says it closed Trump Organization’s accounts after anti-money-laundering review

The disclosure marks the first time a bank has formally tied money-laundering concerns to Donald Trump’s family business. Capital One is seeking to dismiss the case by casting doubt on claims of illegally debanking – or denying services on religious or political grounds – the Trump Organization.

events.title: Heatwave scorching western US ups risk of hazardous fire conditions
events.summary:
In Oregon and Washington, low humidity and powerful winds have put officials on alert for wildfire spread

A heatwave scorching the western US region has elevated the risk of hazardous fire conditions particularly in parts of Oregon and Washington, where low humidity and powerful winds have put officials on alert for wildfire spread.

The National Weather Service has forecast blistering temperatures through early next week that could climb from 110F to 120F across the south-west. In the Pacific north-west, highs reaching into the 90s are expected in the days to come.

events.title: Sopranos actor Vincent Pastore, known for playing mobsters and tough guys, dies aged 80
events.summary:

Vincent Pastore, a veteran actor who played mobsters and tough guys, and was best-known for playing Salvatore “Big Pussy” Bonpensiero on The Sopranos, has died. He was 80.

Bob McGowan, who had managed Pastore since his run on The Sopranos, told the Associated Press that he learned of his death Saturday from another client and actor on the show, Vincent Curatola.

events.summary: Documented cases of violence against LGBTQ+ people in Serbia have never been higher. The attacks are part of a larger shift in society targeting marginalized people.

events.title: Lenacapavir will slow HIV infections if there's enough of it and it reaches at-risk groups
events.summary: Lenacapavir is one injection, twice a year. It's a big improvement for people in high-risk groups, currently taking a pill a day against HIV infection. But its long-term impact depends on it reaching those very people.

events.title: Tour de France final stage shortened due to wildfires
events.summary: Security personnel assigned to the race have been redeployed to help contain major blazes near Bordeaux, reducing Sunday's final stage.

events.title: Germany news: Industry hemorrhaging 15,000 jobs a month
events.summary: Industry boss Tanja Gönner says the situation is critical but offers opportunity. Meanwhile, politicians head to the Bayreuth Festival and security services warn of racist fight clubs. Follow DW for the latest.

events.title: Could 'mesh networks' help overcome authoritarians' internet blocks?
events.summary: In authoritarian countries, the state is often either monitoring online communications or has the ability to shut them down in a political crisis. But there are other ways that activists can keep in touch.

events.title: Eco wins: Cities, creatures, and tech are saving the day
events.summary: From an AI-powered cute little pangolin, heat mapping to cool down cities and animals reducing wildfire risks by doing their thing, these real-world climate hacks are helping communities stay ahead of a changing planet.

events.title: Poland's main opposition collapses over far-right slide
events.summary: A power struggle within Poland's main opposition force has come to a head. But a move to expel former Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki may greatly weaken the right-wing party's popularity.

events.title: Trump threatens EU with tariff probe over Google, tech fines
events.summary: US President Donald Trump has said he will initiate a tariff investigation against the EU in response to fines against US tech companies. He cited the latest case that Google lost on Thursday, as well as others.

events.title: Russia hits drone demonstration near Kyiv, killing 10
events.summary: Ukraine says 10 were killed and around 100 injured in the strike, a day after Zelenskyy met with officials from US arms giant Raytheon. Meanwhile, in St. Petersburg, another Wildberries warehouse came under drone fire.

events.title: Highs and lows as Bayreuth Festival turns 150
events.summary: The Bayreuth Festival's 150th anniversary has been clouded by controversy surrounding German-Jewish speaker Michel Friedman. Yet it offers an opportunity to celebrate, including with an AI-enhanced Ring cycle.

events.title: Why Trump's 'forced labor' tariffs leave the world puzzled
events.summary: After the US Supreme Court struck down Donald Trump's emergency tariffs, the White House has turned to another trade law linked to alleged human rights abuses.

events.title: The trees helping fires spread and what to do about it‌
events.summary: With Spain declaring an emergency, France seeking EU help and Canada dealing with more than 900 hot spots, wildfires are out of control. Monocultures and climate change are partly to blame but can we stop the burning?

events.title: How vanilla's history is not so … 'vanilla'
events.summary: Long before "vanilla" meant bland, the bean's fandom spanned Mesoamerican elites to European courts. But it owes its ubiquity to a 12-year-old enslaved boy.

events.title: Jürgen Klopp and Germany: A partnership long in the making
events.summary: In one of the worst-kept secrets in football, the former Dortmund and Liverpool boss has been named head coach of the German men's national team.

events.title: Klopp named new head coach of Germany men's football team
events.summary: Germany has turned to Jürgen Klopp to lead a new era for the four-time world champions after their disappointing World Cup exit, with hopes of building toward future international tournaments.

events.title: Germany seeks energy and trading partners in Africa
events.summary: Germany wants to boost relations with Africa. During his trip, German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul has promoted cooperation on energy, infrastructure and the economy. He also criticized US treatment of South Africa.

events.title: Sweden eases mining permits to cut China minerals reliance
events.summary: Sweden has declared the mining of critical minerals and rare earths a national security interest. This will ease and expedite the permit process. The government said the step was needed to counter dependence on China.

events.title: Is Germany investing in the right weapons?

events.title: Man dies of injuries after attack at Regensburg bank: police
events.summary: Police say one person has died after sustaining severe injuries at a bank branch in Regensburg. Special units were dispatched and apprehended a suspect armed with a knife.

events.title: Spain's solar eclipse trilogy: spectacle starting August 12
events.summary: From August 2026 to January 2028, amateur and pro sky watchers are in for a series of rare solar spectacles over Spain and North Africa. Astronomers expect the events to attract millions from around the world.

events.title: ECB keeps interest rates unchanged amid Iran war inflation
events.summary: The European Central Bank has kept its base interest rates steady but said it was "closely monitoring" the energy price shock. The impact of the war against Iran on energy costs has pushed inflation over ECB targets.

events.title: Canada-EU: Closer trade ties to counter Trump?

events.title: Oil prices jump as Hormuz, Red Sea crises deepen

events.title: Spain wins second World Cup after beating Argentina in final

events.summary: The Bundesliga has a new home on American screens after Germany's top football league left ESPN. The new deal is a sign of the times.

events.summary: Wildfires are raging across Europe, Canada and beyond. To successfully fight these fires, speed is essential. A German startup uses satellite data and AI to spot fires early.

events.summary: Since millions of NSDAP membership cards have been made available online, many Germans have been surprised to discover that their ancestors weren't always as innocent as family stories had led them to believe.

events.summary: The Welsh singer was best known for the 1980s rock opera hit, along with other songs, including "It's a Heartache."

events.summary: Iran's latest attacks show it can easily disrupt shipping, energy markets and draw in Gulf neighbors. DW asks how much leverage Tehran really has over Washington and if its high-risk strategy could backfire.

events.title: Assassin's Creed: Why pop culture is hooked on pirates
events.summary: Pirates have captured our imagination for centuries. With "Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced," gamers can now head off on another pirate adventure. How has our concept of pirates evolved with pop culture?

events.title: The Australian tree supercharging global wildfires
events.summary: As Europe experiences another summer of extreme heat and wildfire warnings, one tree imported from Australia is coming under renewed scrutiny across the world: eucalyptus.

events.title: Brain tumors: New vaccine offers patients hope for more time
events.summary: A new therapy offers people with seemingly incurable brain tumors scope for hope: It could slow the progression of the disease and extend patients' lives.

events.title: Conflict, climate change, cash-strapped: Why poverty persists
events.summary: With just under five years left to complete the UN's Sustainable Development Goals, a new report shows what's hampering progress. And what the solutions are.

events.title: Heat-resistant housing: How we need to adapt our homes
events.summary: In Germany, it is time to rethink and rebuild. Many apartments were not designed for heat waves. Fortunately, there are ways to adapt existing buildings to the changing climate — but air conditioning isn't the best.

events.title: Why Volkswagen's huge workforce became a costly burden
events.summary: The struggling German carmaker plans to cut up to 100,000 jobs from its 630,000-strong workforce. How did VW's headcount get so bloated, and will the cuts be enough to survive the Chinese EV onslaught?

events.summary: In Germany, where Nazi symbols are banned, activists are using trademark law to fight far-right merchandise.

events.title: Chinese Tianwen-2 space probe reaches asteroid for sampling
events.summary: After a yearlong flight of a billion kilometers, a Chinese space probe is set to take samples from an asteroid. The mission is part of what President Xi Jinping calls the country's "space dream."

events.title: European space telescope Euclid spots oldest quasars yet
events.summary: Think of quasars as time machines. Rare but revealing. They are light from the beginnings of the universe that let astronomers investigate how early galaxies formed.

events.title: Why US train travel lags behind Asia and Europe
events.summary: As flights get pricier and gas prices stay high, more US travelers are turning to trains — and hitting a system built for freight, not people.

events.title: The week in pictures: European wildfires, a woolly mammoth and a migrant influx at Spain's Ceuta
events.summary: Fires burned across much of Europe, an earthquake in Japan killed dozens, record-low water levels in Bulgaria exposed the remains of a woolly mammoth, and tens of thousands sought to cross into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta before eventually returning home: FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the week's most striking images.

events.title: Capital One bank cites money-laundering probe to justify closing Trump Organization accounts
events.summary: Capital One Financial on Friday defended its decision to close more than 300 Trump-affiliated bank accounts back in 2021, stating that it did so after a money-laundering review. The ‌disclosure marks the first time a bank has formally tied money-laundering concerns to US President Donald Trump's family business.

events.title: Hungary: Successive heatwaves drain Danube river used to cool nuclear plant
events.summary: Prolonged drought and extreme heat across Europe have also triggered an energy crisis. For the first time ever, Hungary announced the shutdown of the country’s only nuclear power plant, after water levels in the Danube fell to a record low. Peter O’Brien explains.

events.title: Football: Brentford sign Ligue 1 star Mamadou Sangaré for €48 million
events.summary: Mali's international Mamadou Sangaré is heading to the Premier League following a stellar season with french club Lens. He has officially joined Brentford in a landmark €48 million transfer, setting a new record sale for the French club.

events.title: Colombia police station bombed wounding 14 people
events.summary: Colombia’s government has blamed rebel groups for a truck bomb that wounded 14 people near the border with Venezuela. The attack came less than a week before President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella is due to take office. He has said he plans to end the current administration’s peace negotiations with various armed groups. Morgan Ayre reports.

events.title: Peru: Tourist plane crashes killing all 13 people aboard
events.summary: Eleven foreign tourists and two crew members have been killed after a small sightseeing plane crashed shortly after take-off in Peru. The cause of the crash is not yet known, and an investigation is underway. Peter O' Brien has more.

events.title: Europe to hold meeting Tuesday over Ceuta after migration flux
events.summary: Spain has installed a 500-metre-long sea barrier between its North African enclave of Ceuta and neighbouring Morocco. It comes after tens of thousands of migrants breached the border earlier this week, with at least 67 people dying in the attempt. While most of those who crossed quickly returned to Morocco, the incident has reignited the immigration debate in Europe and beyond. The EU is due to hold an emergency video conference on the issue on Tuesday. Charlotte Hughes reports.

events.title: France: Most of 224,000 evacuees allowed to return home after devastating fires
events.summary: Here in France, a wildfire in the mountainous southeastern Var department, which had been brought under control three days ago, flared up again on Friday, forcing authorities to evacuate nearly 2,500 people overnight. Meanwhile, our reporter James Andre visited Gironde, where France’s biggest wildfire in more than 70 years was recently brought under control.

events.title: Greece: Blazes continue to spread across the country
events.summary: The effects of human-made climate change are being felt across Europe during this sweltering summer, from record heat-related deaths in Austria, Britain, France and Germany, to tinderbox conditions fuelling historic wildfires in Spain, France and elsewhere. Charlotte Hughes takes a look at the situation in Greece.

events.title: Gaza: overnight Israeli strikes kill at least 8
events.summary: Israel carried out overnight strikes in Gaza, killing at least eight people. This is a look at the Strip this Sunday morning. In one attack, an Israeli military helicopter struck an apartment, killing a husband and wife. In another, an elderly man and a child were killed. Earlier on Saturday, at least seven people were killed in strikes that also damaged medical supplies at a hospital. The attacks came after Hamas said it had agreed to the latest stage of a deal aimed at ending the war. Morgan Ayre reports.

events.title: Three people killed in Moscow bombing
events.summary: A blast near the centre of Moscow has killed at least three people and injured 21 others. It happened at around 8pm local time, when a homemade explosive device detonated as a woman tried to enter a restaurant and was stopped by a security guard, according to Russia’s National Anti-Terrorist Committee. Both the woman and the security guard were killed, along with a visitor at the restaurant, which was hosting a private function. Authorities have not said who they believe was the target, but Russian independent media report it may have been a military official. The attack is also suspected of being linked to the war in Ukraine. In recent years, several senior Russian military figures have been assassinated in and around Moscow, with the Kremlin blaming Kyiv for those attacks. Morgan Ayre has this story.

events.title: At least three killed in Moscow restaurant bombing, Russian officials say
events.summary: At least three people have been killed and 21 wounded after a homemade explosive device was detonated at an Italian restaurant in Moscow, Russian officials said late Saturday. Local authorities did not provide any information about who they believe was the target of the attack.

events.title: Middle East live: Trump holds off on striking Iran, calls for 'rapid' deal to end the conflict
events.summary: US President Donald Trump said Saturday that the United States and Israel had agreed to hold off on new strikes on Iran – provided a deal to end the months-long conflict is "rapidly" reached. Iran's acting defence minister said his country would "neither ‌be caught off ​guard nor remain passive" in the face of new US threats. Follow our liveblog for all the latest.

events.title: Spain installs floating barrier in Ceuta after migration influx
events.summary: Spanish authorities said Saturday that they were installing a floating barrier on the sea border between its North African territory of Ceuta and neighbouring Morocco after a surge of tens of thousands of migrants into the territory earlier in the week prompted alarm across the European Union.

events.title: Israeli strikes on residential buildings kill eight overnight in Gaza
events.summary: Israeli strikes on Gaza overnight killed at least eight people after hitting several residential buildings, local authorities said Sunday. Seven people were also killed in Israeli strikes on Saturday, a day after Hamas said it had agreed to the latest deal on ending the war.

events.title: 'A giant of the industry, Purja leaves behind a legacy that inspired a generation to climb higher'
events.summary: Renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja and his nine climbing companions were killed by an avalanche in Pakistan during an ascent of one of the world's highest mountains, his expedition company said on Saturday, as rescuers tackled treacherous conditions to recover their bodies. A giant of the industry, Purja leaves behind a legacy that inspired a generation to climb higher. Click on this video report by Charlotte Lam for more.

events.title: Wiebes wins Tour de France Femmes opener to win first yellow jersey
events.summary: Dutch rider Lorena Wiebes claimed the first yellow jersey of the Tour de France Femmes on Saturday after winning the opening stage in Lausanne, finishing ahead of Mauritian Kim Le Court and European champion Demi Vollering in a sprint finish.

events.title: Russian forces strike targets in Ukraine's Odesa, Mykolaiv ports
events.summary: Russia said on Saturday its forces had struck fuel storage facilities in the Ukrainian port of Odesa and a tugboat used by the Ukrainian military in Mykolaiv. Russia and Ukraine have intensified attacks in recent weeks on Black Sea shipping routes, rattling global grain markets.

events.title: Fast access to Trump's ‘Truth Social’ posts goes on sale for $100,000 per month
events.summary: US President Donald Trump's posts on his Truth Social platform can move markets with a few keystrokes. Starting Saturday, for a fee of $100,000 a month, Wall Street traders can access his "Truth API" service to have high-speed access to the president's announcements about economic policy and global affairs.

events.title: Ceuta: Spain slams "selfish" EU partners
events.summary: Almost all of the migrants who entered Spain’s enclave of Ceuta had left by Saturday, according to officials. An estimated 60,000 migrants entered Ceuta from neighbouring Morocco over just a few days, with at least 67 people losing their lives in the attempt. Spain has announced plans to install a 500-metre-long containment barrier along the sea border. Meanwhile, a majority of EU countries have called for emergency talks in an open letter to the bloc’s interior ministers. Matthew-Mary Caruchet from our France24 International Affairs desk gives more details.

events.title: Ceuta enclave "almost" back to normal after migrant influx

events.title: Scientists study Greenland's melting ice

A team of researchers will spend six weeks investigating whether the loss of glaciers could disrupt a major Atlantic Ocean current system, potentially affecting Europe’s climate. Catherine Viette has more.

events.title: European football body declares no confidence in FIFA's Infantino after World Cup sell-off plan
events.summary: European football's governing body UEFA said Saturday that the president of the sport’s global governing body, FIFA chief Gianni Infantino, had “lost” their "confidence" after his bid to spin off the commercial rights to the World Cup and other competitions into a semi-private company. Infantino had earlier dropped the plan, but the furious backlash it triggered appeared set to upend his presidency.

events.title: Africa: Fighting erupts in Ethiopia's Tigray
events.summary: Clashes between Tigray’s TPLF and the Ethiopian federal army are taking place in a contested area of the northern region, with fears of a renewed war. The last Tigray war, which took place between 2020-2022 left 600,000 dead, and the region has not yet recovered. But mediation attempts from the US and African Union have seemingly failed to prevent the worst. Our correspondent in Addis Ababa Tom Canetti with more.

events.title: At least five dead and dozens missing after Indonesian ferry catches fire

events.summary: The U.S. has agreed to pause attacks on Iran, President Donald Trump said Saturday, amid what he said were the “perimeters of a deal” being agreed upon, which would include the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: Hackers targeted municipal water systems in 7 states this week, FBI says
events.summary: Cyberattacks targeting municipal water systems have been reported in at least seven states this week, prompting the FBI and the Environmental Protection Agency to warn utilities nationwide that hackers are trying to disrupt critical water infrastructure.

events.title: Iran vows to ‘punish the aggressor today’ after U.S. unleashes ‘heavy wave’ of strikes
events.summary: The conflict appeared to draw in new countries, as Egypt confirmed that a drone hit two natural gas vessels at one of its ports.

events.title: Gay cruise denied access to some ports despite booming LGBTQ+ tourism industry
events.summary: Turkey and Egypt blocked a gay-themed cruise from docking at its ports on a recent Mediterranean trip. It's raising questions about how these policies could hurt their economies as the LGBTQ+ tourism industry booms. NBC News' Steven Romo reports.

events.title: Dozens dead in migrant crisis rush into Spanish enclave
events.summary: There are new images surfacing of tens of thousands of migrants rushing into Ceuta, a Spanish enclave, sparking reaction around the world. So far, dozens of people have died in the chaos. NBC News’ Raf Sanchez has the latest.

events.title: Coal mine blast in Pakistan kills at least 32 miners and traps 10 others
events.summary: An explosion inside a coal mine in southwest Pakistan killed at least 32 miners and trapped 10 others underground in what officials believed to be life-threatening conditions as rescuers raced to reach them.

events.title: Spain deploys military to Ceuta after thousands of migrants breach the border
events.summary: Spain is deploying its military to restore order at its border with Morocco in Ceuta after thousands of migrants streamed into the tiny Spanish territory, with at least nine dying in the attempt.

events.title: At least 86 dead after migrants rush into Spanish territory from Morocco
events.summary: Spain was scrambling Friday to contain a sudden border crisis after tens of thousands of people rushed into its North African territory, with dozens killed and political shock waves spreading across Europe.

events.title: U.S. strikes Iran after Trump reportedly issues menacing new threat
events.summary: The fighting shattered a brief period of calm after weeks of escalation between the U.S. and Iran over the strategic Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: K-pop group BTS won’t submit its music for Grammy Awards
events.summary: “I hope that music can be heard and loved for what it is, rather than being divided by region or language,” the group said in a statement.

events.title: At least 13 killed in Japan earthquake as rescuers search for survivors in a ‘race against time’
events.summary: Multiple people were missing a day after a magnitude-7.1 quake struck Kumamoto prefecture, partially collapsing buildings.

events.title: Major earthquake rocks southern Japan, injuring dozens
events.summary: The earthquake, which had an epicenter in the southwest part of the country, was measured at magnitude 6.8 and a depth of 10 kilometers, or just over 6 miles.

events.title: Search for North Carolina woman Liz Waddell is still a missing person case, Grenada police say
events.summary: Grenadian police said their nearly week-old search for a missing North Carolina woman is still active, with hopes of finding the swimmer alive.

events.title: Oil prices slide as U.S. and Iran pause strikes to give ‘space’ for diplomacy
events.summary: The two sides halted fire over the weekend, following 13 nights of attacks that threatened new pain for the global economy.

events.title: Berlin police kill suspect in Pride festival attack after manhunt
events.summary: Authorities say the 21-year-old was fatally shot after charging at officers with a knife, a day after an attack left one dead and 29 injured.
